A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ModeX research and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The algorithms and qualitative examples in v1 Appendices F–G match v2 Appendices H–I.

before.justification: v1 reports original summarization, code-generation, and mathematical-reasoning experiments, including benchmark results, sensitivity analyses, latency measurements, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds SentenceBERT comparisons, component ablations, larger-model evaluations, and GPT-4 results on AIME2025.

M1.justification: The proposed n-gram graph construction, recursive spectral clustering, centroid selection, and ModeX-Lite pruning procedure are unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 are retained; SentenceBERT is evaluated as an additional similarity alternative.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds evaluation on 30 challenging AIME2025 mathematical problems. CNN/DailyMail, HumanEval, and Math-500 remain; the larger-model experiments otherwise retain existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds ModeX–SentenceBERT as a comparison method. The previous ModeX–cosine comparator is renamed ModeX–LastTokenEmb with identical results. Table 1 retains its original comparator set.

E3.justification: Appendix G substantially extends model configurations to Qwen2.5-14B and 32B with N=8, plus GPT-4 with N=8 and 16 on AIME2025. Appendix F introduces controlled n-gram removals at N=8. Existing benchmark subsets, metrics, and main experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E extends the similarity-function analysis with SentenceBERT. New Appendix F tests removing unigrams, bigrams, or trigrams individually on CNN/DailyMail. Existing sensitivity analyses, early-selection evidence, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report Single Path mean ± standard deviation across 16 independent runs in Table 1. Added tables continue baseline uncertainty reporting alongside ModeX point estimates, without introducing new run-count disclosures, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1–2 results and retained Table 3 rows are unchanged. v2 adds substantial results in Table 3 and Tables 4–8, including larger-model comparisons and AIME2025 accuracy of 20.42 for GPT-4 versus 26.67 and 30.00 with ModeX at N=8 and 16. Table 4 adds mixed metric findings: component removal lowers ROUGE but raises BLEU.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorems 1–2, spectral-clustering derivation in Appendix C, and proofs in Appendix D are retained. The added experiments introduce no new formal assumptions, propositions, or derivations.

C1.justification: The central claims remain evaluator-free modal selection, efficient pruning through ModeX-Lite, and strong performance across three task categories. The expanded conclusion restates the existing argument for structured aggregation; the added experiments supply further support.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds an explanation of SentenceBERT versus last-token performance and explicitly rejects universal superiority of lexical similarity. Appendix F interprets higher-order n-grams as contributing richer structure, although its degradation claim overlooks BLEU improvements. The original limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly describes obtaining SentenceBERT sentence embeddings and applying cosine similarity for the added comparison, without specifying a checkpoint. Existing benchmark-selection instructions, prompts, pseudocode, reward-model identifiers, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Choi et al. (2026), When Identity Skews Debate, and Reimers and Gurevych (2019), Sentence-BERT. The broader positioning against evaluator-based selection and closed-ended aggregation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. v2 expands the conclusion and similarity discussion, adds appendix sections and cross-references, and changes numbered citations to author–year citations. Algorithms and qualitative examples are renumbered rather than rewritten.

P2.justification: The main text and much of the appendix change from single-column to two-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating displays. Figure 1 moves onto the first page, Table 3 gains a row, and Tables 4–8 are added. Existing diagrams and qualitative examples retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added similarity comparison, component ablation, and larger-model/AIME2025 evaluations strengthen empirical support for design choices and applicability. Appendix E also qualifies lexical-similarity claims. These benefits are limited by sparse specifications for new configurations and overgeneralized interpretation: Table 4 shows BLEU increasing after component removal despite the accompanying claim of consistent degradation.
